title: Alternating bounded quantifiers
statement: Let $V$ be a language of bit strings, let $m$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, let $b$ be either true or false, and let $w$ be a bit string. At depth zero, the predicate holds exactly when $w\in V$. At each additional level, if $b$ is true it requires some bit string $u$ of length $m$, and if $b$ is false it requires every bit string $u$ of length $m$; in either case the predicate then holds at depth $k$ with the Boolean choice switched and the input replaced by the self-delimiting pairing of $w$ and $u$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of bit strings
